title: Why Stream to Stream inner join doesn't require watermark mandatorily
question:
According to Spark Documentation of Spark Structured Streaming, if 2 tables are stream type, then inner join will work without any watermark however, left outer join requires watermark mandatorily.

I don't understand why. If it is because of state store memory issue (where it might have to store all the data indefinitely), then even inner joins should not be allowed without watermarks, since data size can grow.

From https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/structured-streaming-programming-guide.html#join-operations "While the watermark + event-time constraints is optional for inner joins, for outer joins they must be specified. This is because for generating the NULL results in outer join, the engine must know when an input row is not going to match with anything in future. Hence, the watermark + event-time constraints must be specified for generating correct results."

I don't understand the above statement as well fully. Would be great if someone can explain this.
answer:
You have read the docs I see, and could consult elsewhere.

The manual tells you the answer actually. My take is quite simple:

  1. With inner join, the state is maintained and the assumption that is made that the left- or right-record will arrive eventually (in a subsequent microbatch), or blow up at some time possibly in future - but the records may be kept indefinitely. That said, watermarking is also possible on inner join.

  2. Left outer join states - by definition - that something may not ever arrive, so watermarking is a standard engineering / design practice in Spark Strctured Streaming when doing this.
